title: Stopping at the Unreleased Anchor
statement: Let $B$ be a Boolean finite Turing machine, let $a$ be one of its states, and fix an input word $x$. If $c$ is a configuration of $B$ on $x$ in state $a$, then one step of the stop wrapper from the embedding of $c$ with release bit false and any optional flag $g$ equals the embedding of the same configuration with its state removed, release bit false, and flag set to false.
hypotheses_covered: $B$ is a Boolean finite Turing machine
replaced:
Let $c$ be a configuration of the loop body whose control state is the anchor and whose
release bit is clear. One step of the stop wrapper from the embedding of $c$ halts the
wrapper, writes $\mathrm{false}$ on the flag cell, and changes no other component of the
embedded configuration.
